## Goal

Make the full-campaign arena path the default in batch mode (parent Q3=b) and expose the config/CLI surface: `ArenaConfig`/`BatchConfig` gain a `campaign` surface defaulting to **true**, `scripts/evaluate.mjs` gains a `--skirmish` flag (and keeps `--batch`/`--games`/`--policies`/`--ticks`), a full-campaign run is bounded by a finite tick budget (higher default than the current 1800; `gameComplete`/death ends the run early), and the balance report's existing per-wave/per-level aggregation consumes the new events unchanged.

## User story

As the automated-balancing maintainer, I want `--batch` to automatically exercise the full shipped campaign, so the default report reflects what players experience without extra flags.

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1:** `--batch` and `--games N` with no extra flags play full campaigns and the report shows non-zero `waveReached`/`levelReached`/`upgradesSelected` distributions.
- **AC2:** `--skirmish` opts back into the previous single-level skirmish path (backward compatible for existing consumers/tests).
- **AC3:** Campaign runs are finitely bounded — a configurable tick budget with a sane higher default, early exit on death or `gameComplete` (boss trigger); no unbounded simulation.
- **AC4:** Batch determinism preserved: same seeds + config + policies produce a byte-identical serialised balance report (`recordsHash` stable).
- **AC5:** Single-run evaluation (`runEvaluation`, A/B, human comparison) keeps the skirmish semantics and the difference is documented (report comparability note) — changed only by deliberate later work.
- **AC6:** CLI/engine/report unit tests cover the new defaults and both modes.

## Key Files

**Key Files:**
- `src/ai/eval/types.ts` — ArenaConfig/BatchConfig campaign surface (default true)
- `src/ai/eval/engine.ts` — runBatch campaign default + bounded tick budget
- `src/ai/eval/cli.ts` — --skirmish flag parsing, campaign surface in runConfig
- `scripts/evaluate.mjs` — shell flag wiring (--skirmish, default campaign)
- `src/ai/eval/engine.test.ts` — batch default/campaign/skirmish tests
- `src/ai/eval/cli.test.ts` — CLI flag tests
- `src/ai/eval/report.ts` — per-wave/per-level aggregation (verify unchanged)
data.title: Full-campaign batch runs by default with a bounded tick budget

# Test: wrapAware config plumbing

Test-first verification slice for the `wrapAware` parameter (parent AH-0MV9G3DZ9003P7P8, AC1 + AC5). Pins the data-driven boolean's default, seed exclusions, CSV wiring and editor exposure **before** the implementation item lands, so the pipeline change is driven by failing tests.

## Goal

Pin the full config pipeline for `wrapAware`: default `true`, `march`/`centipede` seeded `false`, CSV persist + round-trip, editor-panel visibility.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A test asserts a generic archetype resolves `wrapAware === true` when the field is absent from its seed config.
- Tests assert the `march` and `centipede` seed configs carry `wrapAware === false` (the explicit exclusion list).
- A CSV round-trip test asserts a `wrapAware` column persists and reloads through the config CSV path; a missing/empty value falls back to `true`.
- A test asserts the field is enumerable through the existing `EnemyConfig` editor/config plumbing without extra per-field admin.
- All tests pass deterministically (no wall clock, no RNG).

## Key Files

- `src/core/configTypes.ts`
- `src/core/configDefaults.ts`
- `src/data/enemy-configs.csv`
- `src/core/enemyConfig.ts`
- `src/utils/csvEdit.ts`

# Field absorbs hits (and rams) before the hull

**Parent:** AH-0MVJ8W4GE007OMNT (AC2).
**Depends on:** Entity field and ram contract tests (AH-0MVM8GTG7002IRTL).

## Goal

As a player, I want a shielded enemy to absorb a few hits behind a barrier
before the ship inside is exposed, so late-game firepower is challenged again
and the barrier-then-hull read is intuitive.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC2 — Force-field absorbs hits before the hull.** A shielded enemy survives its field hits first; every damage source depletes the field, and a ram is absorbed (both survive).
- `BaseEnemy` holds field state (remaining hits), decrements it in
  `takeDamage()` **before** `health`, signals the break exactly once and only
  then lets `health` take damage — no parallel damage path.
- Every player damage source routes through that seam and depletes the field:
  normal bullet, piercing (Wave Laser), AOE weapons, Smart Bomb, Orbital
  Strike, Frenzy bonus hits. A parameterised test asserts at least one case per
  source. Each absorbed hit still **consumes the bullet** (today's behaviour)
  and only the field changes — `health` is untouched until the break.
- Player contact/ram (Q6 = **B**): a shielded enemy's field absorbs the ram —
  exactly **one** field hit per contact, the enemy survives and the player
  survives (no `_hitPlayer`). Implemented once in the shared
  `CombatScene._handleCollisions` step 4, mirroring the Thorn Field
  `tryConsumeThornsRam` precedent, guarded by a documented **shared re-arm**
  constant (recommended ~0.5 s; OPEN QUESTION Q6a in the parent) so a sustained
  overlap cannot drain the field frame-by-frame. Once the field is down the
  existing both-destroyed rule applies unchanged.
- `enemyFactory` threads the resolved hit count into the entity; constructing
  without a field is byte-for-byte today's behaviour.
- `health`, weapon levels, drop rates and the player Shield/Force Field
  power-ups are untouched.

## Key Files

- `src/entities/BaseEnemy.ts`, `src/entities/enemyFactory.ts`.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts` — ram-absorb branch + shared re-arm
  (shared core: the game and every gym inherit it).
- `src/core/constants.ts` — ram re-arm / field constants if not colocated.

# Readable barrier: shared bubble, absorb impact, break cue

**Parent:** AH-0MVJ8W4GE007OMNT (AC3).
**Depends on:** Entity force-field layer (AH-0MVM8GUZG008AWSU).

## Goal

As a player, I want to see a barrier on shielded enemies and to get clear
absorb/break feedback, so I can read "barrier first, hull second" at a glance.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC3 — Readable feedback.** Shielded enemies render a shared bubble drawn by `CombatEffectVisuals`, with absorb impact and a distinct break flash/cue.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatEffectVisuals.ts` gains a shared enemy-force-field
  bubble helper plus exported constants (colour, line width, radius factor,
  fill/stroke alpha). The colour is visually distinct from the player Shield
  bubble (`SHIELD_BUBBLE_COLOR` 0x3399ff) and the player Force Field bubble
  (`FORCE_FIELD_COLOR` 0x33ffcc).
- `BaseEnemy` draws the bubble while its field is up and removes it on break;
  the draw is delegated to the shared helper so the game and every gym render
  it identically (no per-scene copies).
- Each absorbed hit triggers the **existing** shared impact feedback; the
  breaking hit runs a distinct break flash and an audio cue registered in
  `src/audio/effects.ts` (reuse an existing cue where one already reads
  correctly — record the decision).
- Unit tests cover the helper's draw calls/constants (`CombatEffectVisuals.test.ts`)
  and the entity's bubble lifecycle (present while shielded, gone after break).
- No new player-facing UI beyond the in-game bubble.

## Key Files

- `src/scenes/core/CombatEffectVisuals.ts` (+ `.test.ts`).
- `src/entities/BaseEnemy.ts` — bubble draw/removal hooks.
- `src/audio/effects.ts`, `src/core/constants.ts` — cue + colours.
data.title: Shared force-field bubble feedback

data.comment:
Implementation complete — enemy force-field layer (AC2).

Commit: 82c9de81 on `dev` (pushed).

**What landed**
- `BaseEnemy` now owns the field layer: `forceFieldHits` / `hasForceField` / `lastHitAbsorbed` / `forceFieldBroken`, with `takeDamage()` depleting the field **before** `health` and signalling the break exactly once. The `BaseEnemyConfig.forceFieldHits` default of `0` keeps every existing enemy byte-for-byte unchanged. Every player damage source (bullet, piercing, AOE, Smart Bomb, Orbital Strike, Frenzy bonus hits) already routes through `takeDamage()`, so all of them deplete the field with no parallel path.
- `enemyFactory.createEnemyFromConfig(..., forceFieldHits?)` threads the resolved count into the entity (the factory never evaluates the level curve); all 13 archetype configs forward it to the base.
- Shared ram absorb in `CombatScene._handleCollisions` step 4, plus the carried-over-survivor ram path in `PlayScene`, so the game and every gym behave identically.
- `ENEMY_FIELD_RAM_REARM_MS = 500` (Q6a): **answered in the recommended way** — one field hit per ram **contact**, a dedicated 0.5 s re-arm (not the post-hit invulnerability window). Inside the window a fresh overlap consumes nothing and does not hurt the player; once the field is down the pre-existing both-destroyed rule (AH-0MTV7JOLU006W8PT) applies unchanged.

**Decision — ram ordering.** `onPlayerRamsEnemy()` destroys the enemy and runs kill accounting in the game and the generic gym, so it can only run on branches that really destroy the enemy. Step 4 now resolves: Thorn Field (precedence, enemy dies, player unhurt) → enemy force field (one field hit, both survive, **no kill accounting**) → normal ram (enemy dies, player hit). The Thorn-Field-precedence contract test still holds unchanged.

**Test correction (documented).** Flipping the contract tests from `it.fails` to `it` exposed one latent harness-timing flaw in the re-arm-expiry contract test (`src/scenes/core/CombatScene.test.ts`): `advanceGame()` anchors its fixed steps to a fresh wall-clock reading rather than the scene clock's last value, and the deterministic boot already settles ~150 ms, so 600 ms of steps was not guaranteed to land past the 0.5 s re-arm (it failed under load in the full integration run). The advance is now 1000 ms — a pure harness-timing fix; the semantic assertion (a ram after the re-arm consumes the next field hit) is unchanged.

**New coverage.** `src/scenes/core/enemyForceFieldDamageSources.test.ts` — a parameterised test driving each of the six player damage sources through the shared scene paths against a **real** `BaseEnemy`, asserting the field loses exactly the resolved damage, `health` is untouched and the enemy stays alive.

**Verification.** Full suite at the pushed commit: 306 files / 6786 tests (unit + integration). Changed-scope gate green; duplicate-body/gym-parity guard green.
